claims.text: Machine-learning potentials can be integrated with thermodynamic integration or metadynamics to calculate high-temperature fusion free energies.
The proposed method will reduce computational cost by approximately one to two orders of magnitude.
The proposed method will faithfully capture vibrational contributions in both solid and fluid phases.
The proposed method will faithfully capture anharmonic contributions in both solid and fluid phases.
The proposed method will faithfully capture electron–vibration contributions in both solid and fluid phases.
Elemental, binary, and multicomponent high-entropy alloy systems near fusion exhibit significant vibrational and anharmonic behavior.
The ML potentials will be trained on ab initio datasets and coupled to high-temperature free-energy sampling.
Specialized descriptors and uncertainty quantification will map ab initio free-energy landscapes while retaining solid- and liquid-state structural features relevant to entropy.
Uncertainty measures will permit on-the-fly validation and correction of ML predictions.
Replacing explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics sampling with corrected ML predictions will accelerate mapping of free-energy surfaces.
Surrogate-assisted sampling will retain the fidelity of complex entropy contributions while reducing runtime.
The method should be 10 to 100 times faster than explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
The method should match or exceed TOR-TILD accuracy for free-energy differences in complex multicomponent systems.
The method should accurately reproduce melting temperatures and latent heats in complex multicomponent systems.
Previous explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics and TOR-TILD studies in elemental and binary systems demonstrated high fidelity at substantially greater computational cost.
The method is expected to apply from elemental and binary systems through multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Extreme anharmonicity and compositions far outside the ML training set may increase prediction uncertainty.
Nonlinear enhancement of electron–vibration coupling beyond the training regime may require additional corrections.

contradictions.description: The rule describes an acceptable free-energy-error threshold using '>5% deviation,' but also requires errors to remain 'within' approximately 5% bounds. These directions conflict: a fidelity criterion would ordinarily specify no more than 5% deviation, whereas '>5%' denotes exceeding the bound.
